title: Birbal and the Thief's Beard
summary: When a courtier's gold purse disappears during a crowded festival, Birbal uncovers the thief by making a casual remark about beards.
full_text:
During the vibrant festival of Nauroz at the Agra palace, nobles and ambassadors from across the empire gathered to exchange gifts and celebrate. Amid the feasting, a wealthy courtier named Mirza Farooq gasped in shock: his embroidered purse containing fifty gold mohurs had been stolen from his silk sash!

The chamber doors were locked immediately, and fifty suspect attendants and guests were detained. Akbar was frustrated: 'Search everyone!'

Birbal stepped forward: 'Sire, searching fifty noblemen will cause offense and take hours. Allow me to consult the ancient art of physiognomy.'

Birbal walked along the line of suspects, looking calmly into each man's eyes. Then he announced in a casual, carrying voice: 'The thief is foolish indeed. He believes he is safe, yet he does not realize that a tiny white straw from the floor carpet has stuck to his beard!'

Instantly, one of the attendants reflexively raised his hand to brush his chin!

Birbal grabbed the man's wrist: 'Here is your thief!'

The attendant fell to his knees in terror, pulled the gold purse from inside his sleeve, and begged for mercy. Akbar laughed and congratulated Birbal for catching the culprit through the sheer power of human anxiety.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
